api:
<FlameGraph> shows a CPU, memory or time profile three ways: as a flame graph, as a top table of the heaviest functions, and as an expandable call tree. It can compare two profiles too. It's a port of Grafana's Flame Graph; see Coming from Grafana.

use blenderui::prelude::*;
use bui_charts::*;

The buttons' icons are line icons bui-charts draws itself: nothing to register.

layout, color_scheme and text_align set the starting state. After that, the header and toolbar controls change them.

Profile

A profile is a call tree: each frame (a function in a call stack) has a total value, which includes everything it called, and a self value, which is only its own work.

ConstructorUse it for
Profile::from_folded(text)Folded stacks: one line per stack, frames separated by ;, then a count, e.g. main;parse;lex 42. This is what perf + stackcollapse, cargo flamegraph / inferno, py-spy --format raw and async-profiler -o collapsed produce. A total root frame is added on top.
Profile::from_nested_set(rows)(level, label, value, self) rows in depth-first order, Grafana's profile format. Level 0 is the root.
Profile::diff(&baseline, &comparison)Two profiles merged into a diff: matching stacks line up, and each frame keeps both values.
Profile::diff_from_nested_set(rows)(level, label, value, self, value_right, self_right) rows that are already a diff.
MethodReturns
is_diff()whether the profile compares two profiles
len() / is_empty()the number of frames

Labels are stored once per distinct name, however many frames use them.

Panes and layout

PaneShows
Pane::FlameGraphthe flame graph
Pane::TopTableone row per function: Self and Total (or Baseline, Comparison and Diff), sortable by any column
Pane::CallTreethe call tree as an expandable table, with its own search
PaneLayoutMeaning
PaneLayout::Single(pane)one pane
PaneLayout::Split(left, right)two panes side by side, half and half (zopra's divider could be dragged; blenderui has no resizable split); stacked top and bottom when vertical is set

A split layout shows a single pane when the chart is narrower than 800px (unless vertical is set). With header={false} the search box and pane pickers are hidden, so whatever layout you pass is fixed.

Interacting with the graph

ActionResult
hover a frametooltip with the total, self and sample count, as percentages too; Baseline / Comparison / Diff for a diff profile
click a framemenu: Focus block, Copy function name, Sandwich view, your actions, and group expand / collapse
Focus blockzooms to that frame; frames above it are drawn lighter. A pill shows its share and clears the focus.
Sandwich viewshows that function's callers above and its callees below, merged across every place it was called
search boxdims every frame that doesn't match and filters the top table. Separate several terms with commas. Each term is tried as a regular expression first, then as a fuzzy match.
top table search / sandwich buttonssearch for exactly that function / open its sandwich view
call tree up / down arrow buttonsshow that function's callers / callees as the tree
call tree searchfinds functions (case-insensitive; regular expressions allowed), shows "1 of N", and the arrows step through matches, expanding and scrolling to each
Resetclears search, focus and sandwich

Collapsing. When a frame is the only child of its parent and holds more than 99% of the parent's value, the two are grouped onto one row and labelled (N) name. A strip on the left marks groups. Expand or collapse them from the frame menu, or all at once with the toolbar buttons. Set collapsing={false} to give every frame its own row.

Changing data. When data changes, focus, sandwich and grouping reset, unless you set keep_focus_on_data_change.

Colours

FlameColorsColour of each frame
ByPackageby package or module name, so related functions share a colour
ByValueyellow for small frames to red for large ones, relative to the current zoom
Difffor diff profiles: your theme's good colour where a frame shrank, its neutral colour where it stayed the same, and its bad colour where it grew
DiffColorBlindthe same, in blue, grey and red

A diff profile shows a legend from −100% (removed) to +100% (added). Frames too narrow for a label are drawn grey. Set the good, neutral and bad colours in your theme.

Custom menu actions

fn open_source(frame: &Selected<'_>, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App) {
    println!("open {}", frame.label);
}

const ACTIONS: &[FrameAction] = &[FrameAction { label: "Open source", run: open_source }];

<FlameGraph data={profile} actions={ACTIONS} />

Selected gives the clicked frame's label, total, self_value and level.

examples.title: Live profile
examples.description: A signal as data: the graph redraws when it changes.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn live_profile() {
    let profile = use_signal(cpu());
    let round = use_signal(1u32);
    rsx! {
        <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 h-[460px]">
            <div class="cursor-pointer text-sm underline" onClick={move || {
                let next = if round.get().is_multiple_of(2) { CPU } else { CPU_AFTER };
                round.set(round.get() + 1);
                profile.update(|profile| *profile = Profile::from_folded(next));
            }}>
                "Swap profile"
            </div>
            <FlameGraph data={profile} layout={PaneLayout::Single(Pane::FlameGraph)} keep_focus_on_data_change={true} class="flex-1" />
        </div>
    }
}
